Article 6

(4) The procedures, mechanisms and service standards for prevention, protection and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2) and (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Part Four
Form and Mechanism of Prevention and Protection Services Article 8 (1) Policy formulation, program planning and budgeting for prevention and protection services shall be implemented through the following mechanism: a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence; b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with related SKPD;
c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and
d. determination of programs and activities in planning documents. (2) Implementation of prevention and protection services for women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented through the following mechanism:
a. implementation of programs and activities contained in the SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with related SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation and reporting on policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children. (3) The mechanism for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in the Regent Regulation.
(4) Policy formulation, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD responsible for Regional Development Planning.
(5) Prevention and protection efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims shall be implemented by: a. establishing a network in violence prevention efforts; b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders; c. establishing a violence prevention system, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on violence prevention against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

CHAPTER III
OBJECTIVES
Article 3
The objective of implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, is to guarantee the protection of women and children, so that they do not become victims of violence and to guarantee the fulfillment of the rights of women and children as well as families, both before, during and after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur, and prevention so that violence does not occur in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 7

(2) The regional government is obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection against all forms of violence toward women and children and their families.

6.1.rationale: The original Indonesian text (Pasal 5 ayat (1)) mentions coverage “dalam semua situasi termasuk … anak dalam situasi darurat” (children in emergency situations). It does not mention women in crisis/emergency/disaster settings, nor specific measures for women in such settings; the “situasi darurat” qualifier is attached to “anak,” not “perempuan.” The judge overgeneralized from “children in emergency situations” to conclude the policy covers women in crisis settings. Since the retrieved passage accurately reflected the Indonesian and still led to a “Yes,” this is primarily a judge reasoning error rather than translation or retrieval.
